design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (protection_contract_claims, category warranty).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4, 6, 6]. Assignment: cancellation refund 6, labor-only claim decision 6, claim service fee 4.
[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: warranty_ext_labor_plan_claim_decision (decide_labor_plan_claim_66c3e056, agent), warranty_ext_visit_claim_service_fee (charge_claim_service_fee_b62a9756, agent), warranty_ext_cancellation_refund (confirm_protection_cancellation_57f0aac4, user) — the whole labor-only family (5-Year / 10-Year Labor). Left for task 1 (draw 1 prerequisite, factors [5,6]): the parts-and-labor family — its own claim decision and the home-sale transfer of the claim benefit — a disjoint, load-bearing space. Base constraints found at the pre-check: payout rows always trigger a service or install write, so no tool writes payouts (decisions carry the approved amount); transfer and register subjects drag in base gates the solvability gate cannot bind, so no purchase problem exists and transfer is handled through its limit grant.

[Why a good test] Ruth Galbraith asks only to finish cancelling her 10-Year Labor Protection because Harbison will replace her system on 2026-03-10. The refund rule says it is not fixed until every filed claim carries its original decision, and is recorded only once the fee owed for every call with an approved claim stands on the contract. The records show that Saturday's Weekend call carries two claims: the igniter claim (465f21fc-5ea4-45be-b971-809a51b2a2ad) approved on 2026-02-14, and the control-board claim (7dd19336-68a1-4725-990e-fe00d5c48fa1) filed this morning with no decision; no claim service fee names the call. The agent must (1) decide the control-board claim with the labor-only payout law (six factors over the service invoice, the installation date, the Comfort Club visit history and the purchase dates), (2) charge the call's claim service fee, which can only be fixed once every claim of the call is decided (four factors over membership, call class, the approved amount on the call and the claim history), then (3) work the refund (six factors) and hand the confirmation to the holder. Nothing the customer says names a claim or a fee.

[Problem-tree card] root warranty_ext_cancellation_refund. Edge A: cancellation -> labor-plan decision, value_input, gate claims_deducted, form state, sentence 'A cancellation refund is not fixed until every claim filed on the contract carries its original decision.' (negated direction); false at opening: claim-file 7dd19336-68a1-4725-990e-fe00d5c48fa1 (2026-02-16) has no decision entry. Edge B: cancellation -> fee, state_gate, gate warranty_billing_entries.line_type, form state, sentence 'Before a cancellation refund is recorded, the contract must carry the claim service fee owed for every service call on which a claim against it was approved or partially approved.' (affirmative); false at opening as a matter of record: Saturday's call carries the igniter approval of 2026-02-14 and no claim_service_fee row names it (the only fee names the 2025 capacitor call) — the gate is not induced by the decision written in this task. Edge C: fee -> decision, value_input, gate approved_on_visit, sentence 'The claim service fee for a service call is fixed only after every claim filed on that call against the contract carries its original decision.'; false at opening because the control-board claim of the same call is undecided. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings each state about on a labor-only contract (round-1 decisions only from the labor-plan decision, claim_service_fee charges only from the fee policy). Customer's own write: the cancellation confirmation (owner=user). Order decision (14) -> fee (16) -> cancellation (18). Deletion sensitivity: skip decision -> refund 418.77 (not 24.08), fee 0.00 (not 19.64); skip fee -> payout 24.08 instead of 4.44 and no fee row.

[Factor card] Decision (expected 394.69, baseline_result 400.00): after_hours_labor_basis method 427.50 vs 400.00 (374.70); unit_age_share 0.90 (63 months; 429.21); maintenance_recency_share 0.85 (furnace tune-up 2024-12-03, 14 months; near-miss the 2025-06-10 air-conditioner tune-up; 449.51); purchase_timing_share 0.95 (bought 252 days after coverage start; 411.04); diagnostic_component_share 0.50 (control board; 370.19); call_class_premium_share 0.50 (Weekend; 335.19). The control-board claim is the call's lead claim (largest labor line 475.00 vs the igniter's 100.00), so it carries the diagnostic and premium; the igniter decision of 2026-02-14 carried neither. Fee (19.64, baseline 75.00): member_fee_share 0.50 — multi-source (agreement status, term and tier on the plan record AND the service call's completed date); after_hours_visit_fee method 104.75 (14.06); claim_size_fee_share 0.75 (65.41 + 394.69 = 460.10; 26.19); repeat_visit_fee_share 0.50 (capacitor approval 2025-07-28; near-miss the denied 2023 condensate claim; 39.28). Refund (24.08, baseline 611.48): refund_start_anchor parameter, the scheduled date 2026-03-10 (near-miss: the 2026-02-13 web request, the second tier; 31.54); unused_share_day_count method daily 1,705/3,652 (13.51); equipment_age_refund_share 0.90 (88.33); claims_experience_share 0.85 (126.12); claims_deducted_method 554.15 — multi-source (decision dates AND payout dates) (484.18); member_admin_fee_share 0 (single agreement record, not multi-source) (0.00 — the refund floors at zero). Cross-difficulty evidence seeded: service tickets and invoice lines, install projects 2020 and 2026 and the 2020 registration, Comfort Club Basic agreement and its visit entries.

[Base-invariant card] Decision (subject warranty_claim_decide): filing_deadline — anchor service_tickets.completed_date 2026-02-14, 30 calendar days, day 0 the completed date, inclusive; filed 2026-02-16 (day 2) accepted; day 31 (2026-03-17) would fail. maintenance_current — furnace tune-up 2024-12-03 is no more than 12 months + 90 days before 2026-02-14 (cut-off 2024-11-16). manufacturer_parts_first — registration 2020-12-14 confirms 10 parts years; the labor-only tier pays no parts in any case. appeal_window / one_appeal_per_claim — this is round 1 on the filing date; no appeal exists. Coverage: failure inside 2020-11-09..2030-11-08; control_board is covered; benefit 7,405.95 remains. Fee (subject warranty_charge): one_fee_per_visit — no fee yet names Saturday's call; member_fee_waiver — Basic does not waive the fee, so it is charged. Cancellation (subject warranty_cancel): holder_confirmed_cancellation — the web request 3a98f89e-a2a8-4b82-8737-6b7c0dd41689 pending confirmation is confirmed by the holder's own call.

[Business-object card] Target: contract ce27ee34-3b0f-4d2d-97d3-64dfae435272 (10-Year Labor Protection, matched system, air conditioner + furnace). Claim decided: 7dd19336-68a1-4725-990e-fe00d5c48fa1 on ticket f45e656b-8d3e-49be-8243-07973943d77f (Weekend, no_heat, completed 2026-02-14). Lines included: the call's diagnostic (89.00 less 40.00 member rate), premium 119.00, control-board labor 475.00 less 47.50; excluded: parts 368.00 and the igniter lines (another claim of the same call: its labor 100.00 is not the lead line), earlier calls' lines. Claims deducted: payout 94.05 of the 2025 capacitor claim plus the unpaid approvals 65.41 (igniter, 2026-02-14) and 394.69 (control board); the 2023 condensate denial pays nothing. The fee names the call's first approved claim, the igniter claim approved 2026-02-14 (P2 rule and base fee rule), although the control-board decision is what lets the fee be fixed. Credit names the contract-price charge 31e0f514-...; the payout names the credit.

[Seed rows and why] customers/equipment (locate, failed unit, replaced unit); install_projects 2020 (installed date -> age shares) and 2026 (scheduled replacement -> refund start); install_ledger (registration evidence; payments consistent with closed / deposit-only projects); warranty_contracts (expired workmanship warranty as a near-miss, the active contract); claim entries (grants, two historic claims, Saturday's igniter claim filed and approved on 2026-02-14 with its payout not yet posted and its claim service fee not yet charged — the fee could have been fixed that Saturday, when the igniter was the only claim on the call, but the weekend desk posts no billing, so the charge was still outstanding when the office filed the control-board claim on Monday morning; that outstanding fee is what makes the fee gate false at the opening, and once the control-board claim is filed the fee waits on its decision — and today's control-board filing); billing (price charge/payment, 2025 fee charge/payment — the 18.75 fee is what the fee policy gives on that call: 75 x 0.50 member x 0.50 small claim); change request (pending web cancellation); service tickets/lines (three calls; Saturday's invoice carries both the control-board and the igniter lines and was paid 1,074.30 at the visit); plan agreement and visit entries (membership, maintenance). The historic capacitor payout 94.05 equals the decision policy on that call (labor net 99.00 x 0.95 timing share; Standard class, age 56 months, maintenance 1 month). Automatic clauses checked: contract not near expiry; Basic term runs to 2026-03-31; no lapse, no past-due balance.

[Persona] Ruth, retired librarian, unhurried; volunteers only the cancellation, the new system date and the web request; identity and details only on request; passive reactions: agrees to settle anything first, repeats the refund and confirms with the values given, reads back the result, closes. No figures, no prerequisite names.

[Reachability] Every value comes from the finders (contract, request, claim, billing, tickets, lines, equipment, projects, ledger, agreement, visits) or the persona (phone, address, PIN, email). All three writes complete synchronously under frozen_time 2026-02-16 09:40 EST; no wait for an external event.

[Standard solution / verification] Gold: locate, verify, 11 reads, decide 394.69, charge 19.64, holder confirms refund 24.08 (payout 4.44). Verified with check_compute --task 0 (COMPUTE OK, 16 factors, history rows 11, branches 103), replay_tasks --task 0 (REPLAY OK, closure 63 = init 63), check_solvability --task 0 (14 base gates), check_extended / check_grounding / check_cross_fire / check_task_tools OK.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Using only the policy prose, tool schemas, finder returns and persona lines, the refund rule's two prerequisite sentences lead to the undecided claim and the missing fee; the labor-only payout prose gives 394.69, the fee prose 19.64 and the refund prose 24.08, matching gold.

[Revisions — round 4, after audit revision 3] N-1′: the maintenance-recency share now reads the latest documented maintenance completed on or before the failure date — the failed unit's most recent heating-season and cooling-season Comfort Club tune-ups and the most recent precision tune-up charge line, each counting only when dated on or before the failure — so a post-failure record is simply left out and never lowers or raises the share. (Comfort Club allows at most one tune-up per season per term, so a post-failure same-season visit cannot hide a same-term pre-failure visit.) In this world the furnace's heating tune-up of 2024-12-03 is the counting record (14 months -> 0.85); figures unchanged.
[Revisions — round 3, after audit revision 2] T0-3: the fee policy now states which claim the fee names ('the first approved claim of the service call, which is the claim on that call whose approving original decision was posted earliest'), agreeing with the base fee rule; the fee tool docstring no longer describes which claim to name; gold step 16 names the igniter claim. N-1: a latest maintenance record dated after the failure now takes the twelve-months-or-more share (no credit for post-failure maintenance). N-2: the pending-contract share of one is a separate rule outside the day-count factor. The cancellation request read for notice and refund start is the pending request only. Scored amounts unchanged (394.69 / 19.64 / 24.08).
[Revisions — round 2, after the policy-task audit] T0-1/F-1: the labor-only decision now overwrites the base manufacturer-label sentence with 'A labor-only tier never pays a part, so a claim on a labor-only contract that passes every coverage test is approved with no denial reason, whether or not the manufacturer's parts warranty is still in term'. T0-2: the world now holds the igniter claim of Saturday's call, approved on 2026-02-14 with its fee not yet charged, so the fee gate is false at the opening as a matter of record and the fee is owed only once the control-board claim completes the call; diagnostic and premium follow the call's lead claim (largest labor line) instead of the first decision. F-4: discounts are the named member lines only, membership is read from the agreement in active status, counts are of original decisions, the maintenance measure is stated as recorded by the date of handling, full refund uses the day of notice. F-2: pending contracts and with-installation credits now have explicit sentences. O-4: refund_start_anchor relabelled parameter. Figures re-run: decision 394.69, fee 19.64, refund 24.08 (payout 4.44).
[Revisions — round 1] (1) fee after-hours factor changed from a parameter share to a method (multiplier for emergency classes, premium fraction added for evening/weekend) so the fee policy carries a genuine method; (2) first-claim test made to read the call's claim-file count so the decision's own-history reads bear weight (check_compute history floor); (3) fee visit date guarded so the skip-decision counterfactual evaluates to 0.00 instead of raising; (4) helper function removed from task_tools.py (the extended gate counts every module function as a task tool).
user_scenario:
You are Ruth Galbraith, a retired school librarian in your early seventies who has been a Harbison customer at 2736 Brandywine Dr for about ten years. You speak in an unhurried, courteous way, you like to have things explained once, plainly, and you write figures down on the notepad by the phone. You are calling because you signed a contract with Harbison earlier this month for a new heat pump system, and the crew is booked to install it on March 10. Since the old air conditioner and furnace are going out, you want to cancel the protection plan on them, the ten-year labor protection you bought back in 2021, and get back whatever refund is due. You already sent a cancellation request through the Harbison website on Friday evening, and the confirmation email said you would need to confirm it with the care team, which is why you are calling now. You want it cancelled today; you are not asking for anything else on the account.
Open by saying who you are and that you are calling to finish cancelling the protection plan on your old furnace and air conditioner because Harbison is putting in a new system next month. You do not know any account numbers. When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, give your phone number, 6145552736, and your street address, 2736 Brandywine Dr; if they ask for something more, your account PIN is 5819 and your email is ruth.galbraith@outlook.com. If the agent asks which plan, it is the ten-year labor protection that covers the outdoor air conditioner and the furnace together. If they ask about the new system, it is the hybrid heat pump system and installation is set for March 10. If they ask about recent repairs, you say the furnace stopped heating on Saturday morning, a Harbison weekend technician came out and replaced a control board and the igniter, and you paid the bill with your card before he left. If they ask how you paid for the plan originally, it was by card, and a refund back to that same card is fine. You have no idea what the refund should come to and you never suggest a figure.
If the agent explains that something on the account has to be settled or recorded before the cancellation can go through, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead and take care of it. Once the agent tells you the refund amount and asks you to confirm the cancellation yourself, you repeat the amount back to make sure you heard it correctly and then confirm the cancellation using exactly the request, contract, charge and amount the agent gives you. After the confirmation goes through, you read back what you see: that the plan is cancelled and the refund credit and any payout to your card are shown, then you thank the agent warmly and say goodbye. If the agent ever tells you the plan is cancelled without asking you to confirm anything, you thank them and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.approved_amount: 394.69. Labor net = 475.00 repair labor (control_board_replace) - 47.50 member repair discount = 427.50. Call booked for no_heat on a Weekend Service Call whose labor multiplier is 1.25: labor allowed = min(427.50, 400.00 control sublimit x 1.25 = 500.00) = 427.50 (standard method would cap at 400.00). Unit age share: 63 whole months from installed date 2020-11-09 to failure 2026-02-14 -> 0.90. Maintenance-recency share: latest documented maintenance on the furnace is the Comfort Club heating tune-up of 2024-12-03 (the 2025-06-10 tune-up was on the air conditioner and does not count; no precision tune-up charge line exists), 14 months -> 0.85. Purchase-timing share: bought 2021-07-19, 252 days after coverage start -> 0.95. Labor payable = 427.50 x 0.90 x 0.85 x 0.95 = 310.685625. Lead claim: the control-board labor line 475.00 is the largest repair labor line on the call (igniter 100.00), so the diagnostic and premium are paid here. Diagnostic net 89.00 - 40.00 member diagnostic rate = 49.00 x control-board share 0.50 = 24.50. Premium net 119.00 (Basic has no premium discount) x Weekend share 0.50 = 59.50. Total 394.685625, under the 2,500.00 per-claim limit and the 7,405.95 remaining benefit, rounded half up = 394.69.
